t:
Astro what labe?

Look how skilled ancient crafters were! Today all you have to do is press the buttons to rule the ship. Back in the old days, a good captain could navigate through the Astral with his eyes closed. Let me take a closer look at your astral labe.

Right, I know the place. Look, this figure is called a coordinate. In this place there’s a small allod with Imperial dogs on it. No idea what they do there. Some kind of scientific ex-perdition, or something. Anyway, Queen said don’t bother the Imperials, but don’t let them in Umoir, either - they signed a peas tree, whatever it is.

By the way, we have a real Xadaganian here! True story, you know, he’s a swindler and an easy rider, and a traitor, too - he’s fleeing from Imperial justice. No wonder about that. The Imperials tend to hang every other criminal, so it’s pretty understandable. Queen ordered to protect him, anyway.

Where to find him, you ask? Talk to the guards, I’ve seen them dragging him into jankers.
You love so gloomily and with distress, but a woman's love is light and wild. Who to a young girl's heart and face would say, "Love one, and never change"?

r95304.s: Head Mechanic of the House de Ardeur

t:
Welcome back to the world of living... Even though it may sound ironical.

Let me introduce myself. I am Sarbaz Sais, a researcher of the Church.

So Nefer Ur sent you? Interesting. After all these years, he still... Hah.

Welcome to the Citadel, as the locals call it. It is inhabited by demons and Demonologists, the pioneers of the new magical discipline. Or at least that's how they see themselves. The Church sees them as dangerous renegades. I share this opinion, but I'm not here to judge anyone. My interest is purely academic...

Well, since you're well and in good health, that's one load off my mind. I can work on my research now.
Play cards? Hmm, perhaps I should have some fun?
h: Your Majesty, would you like to go to the casino?

t: Eh, things were different during my rule... The nobility was more noble, and the bourgeoisie was more modest.

Oh, hello, ! You're here, too!

Check out the stuff my boss came up with. I helped him!
You’re not allowed to talk to prisoners! If you have questions, well, ask me!
Danil pointed at him, said he was the thief. What he stole, I don’t know, and it’s none of my business. My task is to catch the thief! Go to Danil and ask him, if you want.
You can get an answer, but in this world, knowledge has shape. Will you sacrifice the integrity of your soul for this?
The guardian of the Show Stele is silent.

Then listen... This is a very old story. I am the one who was enslaved.

No one expected the uninvited guest. An eternal wanderer, a rolling stone, he came from afar before Mother and Father's court.  Having been warmly welcomed, he soon came into his own, possessing a sharp tongue and a keenness for various amusements.

However, all that was only part of his act. He never told the whole truth, but shunned outright lies, and so he gradually entangled some of us in his nets. And the day came when the former order collapsed. The world shifted and we could only observe in desperation the events of the time of troubles, which brought with it the Great War.

One person who believed him was my sister. And the day came when I decided to bring her home. I was naive and pure, and I went to his Kingdom myself. Gathering my strength, I stood before the great gates and called. The gatekeeper answered me: “Why do you come here, Daughter? Don’t you know you stand before the gates of the Kingdom of no return?”

And I answered that I came for my sister. The gates opened and I entered, but never left. From that moment on, he became a foster father to me, and I his obedient daughter, like my sister. And as my foster father planned his great work, so he put all of me into it, and I became the Soul of his work.
But not in our world! You can't even die properly here, let alone resurrect. But you can use your Patronage abilities. They are so weird...

My logic is this... All-Mother accepted you, right? She did. Which means you're not our enemy. And you have plenty of leather equipment, and it would be difficult to barter with you. So I found a solution.
h: Why do you trade with us?

t:
The thing is... The portal is functional, you see, but the power source died a long time ago... Don't worry, I thought of everything while you were flying among the clouds. Do you see idols on the sides?

They don't really serve a purpose, but there's energy inside them that we could use...

If you find me about a dozen energy crystals, it should be enough for the portal.
h: What's the matter? Do you need help?

t: Wait, I need to insert the crystals...
Keeping an eye on you! Can't leave you on your own even for a minute! Just look around you...
h: Erfar! What are you doing here?

t:
It's nice to be back home... I've had enough of the cold and gloomy Gipat, sorry.

Suslanger! The nights are as hot as the days; there are camel caravans, palaces, sands, and ancient magic! There are so many things here!

Of course, I'd like to be... more alive. I hope we'll remedy that in our future adventures...
h: How do you like it on Suslanger?

t:
I've been thinking... what would I do on Gipat? I have no one to wait for, and then there's you... and adventures... I'm not that ancient yet, I might still be of use!

I see you're in trouble? At least you have a friend!
h: Erfar! How did you get here?

t:
Buddy! What brings you here?

I’m a nobody, even if I were a village elder at some point. But it's nice to attend a celebration now and then.

Buddy! What brings you here?

I wanted to see what all the fuss was about, and since the jinn came here, I followed him.

Things are quiet on Suslanger. The Orcs calmed down a bit, and the adventurers chased away those who kept them from finding the treasures.

I have also discovered something interesting... Perhaps I will tell you later.

Listen, you’re talking to all these Great Mages, and I’m a nobody, even if I were a village elder at some point. Can you put in a word for me? I need one little thing - a dragon's heart.

Did you think Empress Hirkalla was out of the picture? No, the Empress ordered me to closely watch anyone who would speak against her!

And has not revoked her decrees, she expects them to be upheld! Fortunately, she has not just monsters, but also the loyal guard on her side.

However, if you find yourself in the southern regions of Jigran, see if the Elder is as powerful as they say and if he needs new servants with experience - in managing a village, searching for precious metals, infiltrating secret organizations, espionage and disinformation...

You're carrying a particle of the God of Light with you. Ask for his help!

I'm sure he will try to trick you, knowing his temper. But you know best what's in your head, right?
Nothing that you wouldn't know already. It's Darkness. Infinite Darkness.
The old man in dark clothes is smiling kindly at you. His face looks slightly familiar.
The old man is eyeing you, floating above the ground.

quests: Equipment Upgrading Tutorial: Scroll of Enchantment

t:
I am one of the oldest living Children of this Tree.

Yes, we are the Children of the Tree and the All-Mother. Each Tree gives rise to its own tribe. And each of the Children can give birth to a new Tree. They are long-lived but not immortal, like everything created by the All-Mother. A Tree lives for ten thousand seasons, and then it dies. But while it lives, the Tree gives birth to fruits - and we are these fruits.

We do not live as long - only for about fifty years - and when we die, we ourselves become the germs of future Trees. Not every germ is destined to sprout, but those that succeed will gain great honor and glory.

Every morning I bless our creator for her wisdom and kindness.
h: Hello, what do you do here?

t: Our life is only a moment compared to the life of a Tree...

Ah, it's you...

They let everyone in these days!

Ah, it's you...

Well, are you happy? Did you get what you wanted? Saved Skulnar from Elleken?

My father has plans that go far into the future. I tried to warn Zayan, but he refuses to listen to me...

You know, I acted in his interests for so many years, but as soon as I stumbled, he was quick to forget about me. It made me rethink what I believed about everything happening in our world, and my mother's actions started making sense.

I want to protect Sarnaut from Nihaz. These gods do not belong here.

If we have to use Skulnar, so be it.

I'm not going to put up with the Darkness in Sarnaut, whatever the motives of this Hirkalla. I'm sure we can handle it ourselves, because you and the others have managed to challenge and defeat even more powerful creatures so far!

Since you were able to thwart her plans in Eden, maybe you can do it here, too?

I need to talk to Zayan - together we can work something out.

Yes, it couldn't be otherwise! I knew you would not buy into the promises of Catherina and this psychopath Felix. The Children are in the right. As for the All-Mother - yes, you can and should disagree with her, but opposing her? Indirectly helping Nihaz and Hirkalla? That would plunge all worlds into darkness!

Hirkalla has violated all the laws - both divine and human, and who knows what this will lead to? The dead have awakened, our allods are plunging into nightmares, and something is happening to the Great Trees...
h: It was nice to fight side by side with you.

t:
I'm sorry this happened! But I hope you can see now that the All-Mother was partly right.

Hirkalla has violated all the laws - both divine and human, and who knows what this will lead to? The dead have awakened, our allods are plunging into nightmares, and something is happening to the Great Trees...

We must stop her at all costs, find allies who will agree to challenge her!
h: It's too bad we fought on different sides

t:
Hah, you've come up with a lot of plans! Everyone will have their own idea of how to deal with Tep... But I have something, too. And I understand dark magic, trust me! My father is probably not the only mage in this poor world, right?

Zayan won't tell you this, but believe me - the elves witnessed Hickut's death, but not the fate of the Junes who had fallen victim to Sarn's curse back in the day.

The Conclave, when they were convinced the Plague was gone, could not leave all these artifacts and grimoires lying freely accessible in the dead cities. The expedition they assembled took everything that was even remotely dangerous. Where do you think it ended up? And how did Armando's father, Gramont, came up with that spell?

Yes, these powerful items are somewhere on Nocturne... Maybe I should visit it? They say the House de Douceur has some problems there...

Have you dealt with the orc down there? Praise Tensess, I'm so sick of dying every time I try to escape! Death isn't a joke, you know. It's a very painful stage of life! But it's over now... The love of my life and I can leave this place now!

[... ...Evgeny abruptly turns to his companion and interrupts her rudely:

Yes, I do know which way to go!
h: [The young man in black nods to you politely.]

t:
Friend! How are things?

We are faithful guards of Great Queen Catherina. We joined the Circle of the Keepers to help them fight the Blight. Al Rihat is the last frontier separating the free lands from the infection that's devouring our country. While the Blight started to retreat thanks to your victories, the triumph is still far away.

Shhh... Don't tell anyone... I can... You know what I can do, right? I can help you with something... I can help you get experience... Lots of experience... Do you want to use my services? Go right ahead, but just don't tell anyone...
Good luck, my friend. Come back if you ever need anything!

You want to know about the Stalwart clan? Well, we're far from modest, so we'll tell you everything!

In short, our clan is the largest on Isa. Back in the day, our ancestors battled that Orc clan - the Northwind one! As you can see, we live here in Skalgard.

The Stalwarts also form the hird, the Gibberling battle unit. Representatives of any clans can join it, and if circumstances require, all of Isa's Gibberlings! All our warriors knows how to fight since their childhood - be it with a sword, a frying pan, or a fishing harpoon. The smallest ones can take out an enemy with snowballs!

Hird is not just an army, but also a second family. Our warriors and rogues form the backbone of the clan, and their favorite weapons are axes and hammers. Our most effective tactic is to swarm the enemy! Of course, we're not some tree-sized Jotunns, and our small size forces us to be cunning and actively help each other in combat. But together we're a formidable force!

Our clan has its own secrets, such as the ability to enter a berserk state, which makes our warriors true killing machines! All in all, in combat we rely on cunning and any means at hand, sometimes unexpected ones. If all else fails, we will pile in and overwhelm the enemy!
Hey, where are you going? Come back here!

r475619.s: Surrounded by a pile of dead bodies

t: A cute fluffy animal. There are dead bodies and blood everywhere. It was probably not involved.
h: A cute and innocent-looking hare looks at you from the ground, surrounded by a pile of dead bodies. Something is not right.

t: Look at my owls! Aren't they amazing!
Here's Brownie! She's the fastest in the forest, at night she can spot a mouse from over 300 steps away!
Here's Snowflake! She's the toughest - she can even bring a young deer... If she finds one, of course...
Magic Horse stamping its hoof impatiently.
As the girl comes up to Roan, it calms down.
h: Ask Milava to soothe the horse

t:
Greetings! Greetings! Welcome to what's known as Al Rihat Ruins now.

Why is that? There was a great city here once, it was called Al Rihat. It perished even before the Blight, during Skrakan's time when another war with the Orcs began. It was led by Tugarin, one of the last giants.

You can see these ruins in the western part of these lands. They are now the very heart of the Blight. And here we have an elven settlement, once the fiefdom of a small elven House de Tristesse.

But perhaps you want to know more about what we have here?

I can tell you what my brothers from the Circle said... Of course, the information might be a little... outdated...

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

Right behind the temple district, near the tombs, there was an arena where the heroes fought for glory for people's entertainment. When the city fell, the heroes of former days who rested nearby rose from the ground to defend their hometown. Or so they say. I don't know whether it's true or not. But there are a lot of fighters who have risen from the ashes around here!

There are dead people wandering around the place, but the living are still more dangerous. Beware of Netweavers and Dropplers, and if you see a rat queen, give it a wide berth!

Fear reigns here alongside sadness. You can't go very far these days without running into a ghost mourning its hometown. Aside from them, there are Corpse Eaters and Smokeshrooms. I hear marauders make chowder out of them. Well, what's there to say? Bon appetit!

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«It is said that there were countless temples throughout Al Rihat. People prayed to all sorts of deities in there - both known and unknown lest they offend someone. And yet, when the horde came, prayers did not save the city. Tiny shrines, or the giant Pantheon - everything is in ruins now.

The most formidable monsters that live here are not ghosts. Asura is more terrifying, and the mantes are angrier. And meanest of all is our brother, the man. Watch out for the marauders, they are everywhere these days!

I heard newcomers here tell each other legends about the hideous Gazebo. What do they know! There's no need to be scared of Gazebo: it's not a monster at all, more like a gazebo-shaped structure. Ghosts are the ones you should be worried about. Many people lived here, many still wander around, howling and wailing.»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«They look pretty, those crystals, but when they cover the ground like a scab, it's not a pleasant sight. People used to live here, there were children running around. And now these things are sticking out of the ground.

Beware of the beasts of the forest - the altered ones. Dropplers, Gulpers, and all that. We also have mantes here now. They'll eat you and won't leave any bones!

The monsters here are mostly living. There are Hydras, Mewks, and even mantes. They might be hideous, but when you meet a few ghouls or the dreadful Gazebo, you'll start to miss them!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«They say the elves have great houses, and Tristesse was one of them, but they were considered poor. Well, I don’t know. If you ask me, most would be lucky to be that "poor". Look at the towers they built! They also had strong warriors and powerful sorcerers. If only Catherina hadn’t turned the people of Umoir against them, they wouldn’t have let the Blight into these lands, and the Lulleaguin stronghold wouldn’t have fallen. Well, other elves live in their houses now. They are from a great house apparently. To hell with that greatness, I say!

Ghouls may be scary, but even they are afraid of someone. The necromantic curse was put on them, and the mother earth really doesn't like it. The Satyrs come here to hunt them, and spiders spin webs around them. And the worst of all are the mantes that sneak up on you unnoticed. Remember: right now, they are a threat both to the bloodsuckers and to you!

Damn, these vampires are so creepy! Even necromancers who deal with dead bodies are wary of them. It's ancient magic, forbidden and bloody... Well, if you go a little further, it's where the forest people dwell. And Werewolves, and Minotaurs. Do not disturb them for no reason - if you think about it, they are not our enemies at all. Except for the Ogres, of course. Show those no mercy!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«It's an old stronghold that remembers Danas himself. It's where our fortress used to be. We guarded the shrine - the great tree. It doomed us when some unfortunate person carried the infection inside. Everyone who stood guard here died in a terrible siege: forest monsters on the outside and blighted Treants on the inside. Now that both the fortress and the tree are gone, the destruction of the entire forest is only a matter of time. If we don't find a cure, in a month or six everything here will be covered with blue scab.

We Keepers have always thought of ourselves as friends of nature. We forgot what mother earth can be like - it can soothe you or kill you. When the Blight first came, the animals and the people of the forest didn't care whether you were a pagan or Catherina's henchman - they took up arms against all humans. Beware of them - and the Satyrs, spiders, and most of all - the mantes!

Once a stronghold of life, the tree has turned into a hotbed of disease. The area around it is teeming with all the horrors we're fighting all over Umoir: both mutated animals and corrupted Treants... And marauders, of course - there's no escape from them!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«The land of Umoir is full of wonders! Here, for example. Look! All year round, hot springs gushed up from under the ground. People from all over the allod came here to relax in the baths. They say Skrakan himself liked to soak his old bones here... Now only a memory of these miracles remains. Healing springs turned into an infected swamp.

The main danger in this area is the marauders. It's warm and cozy for them here, and there is plenty of prey... It's true what they say: a man gets used to anything!

Apparently, it's not just humans who appreciate the bathhouse: both Minotaurs and Werebears love to splash around here. We don’t have time for that while the allod is in danger!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«Isn't it great to get out of the blue haze and feel the green grass and the warm sun again? It's beautiful here: before the fall of the city, country estates stood here, the tower of the sorceress loomed over the city... But it won't be green and bright here for much longer. Sooner or later, the Blight will come here too. And if we don't find a cure, the whole Umoir will die.

If the Blight hasn't reached some areas, it's because mother nature won't let it. But it's not strong enough. Little by little, it gives way under the weight of the disease. And yet it doesn't give up. To any animal, any Satyr or Werewolf here, you are nothing but a carrier of infection. Do not try to negotiate with them, they will not listen to you. If they attack, steel your heart and defend yourself!

Even if it’s not as terrible here as in the ruins of the city, even if the ground is yet unaffected by the disease, the bones of the townspeople still crunch under our feet. It was a terrible battle. Oh, so terrible. And there are just as many ghosts here, outside the city, as there are on the ruined streets. Have pity on them: help the unfortunate find peace if you can!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«This was a holy place. Maybe it's thanks to these ancient stones that the Blight hasn't reached it yet. But their strength is running out. A little more - and the place where people lived, rejoiced, and prayed will be buried under the blue mold.

Even a simple beast in this place is formidable. It's an old grove, the holy of holies of mother earth! They are children here, and we are stepchildren. They are the hosts, and we are uninvited guests!

Treants, Werebears, and Spiritwoods live here. And the monsters... There are no monsters here. Get this through your head! We are the Blighted vermin here! Listen to me: if I hear that you bully our Spiritwoods, you'll regret it!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«The townspeople would lose their minds if an astral ship fell in the middle of the city! But there had been no park or townspeople here for a while when it happened. I don't know whose ship it was or what destroyed it. There's no sign of the crew, and the cargo, if there was one, was plundered by marauders a long time ago. They say every now and then the smell of smoke or cooking wafts from the thing. If you find out who the cook is, make sure to tell me!

In these parts, try to avoid Asura. If it puts a hex on you, there'll be no lifting it! I've also heard about forest witches in the area. If it's true, then we're in deep trouble... I pray you won't meet them!

The area is swarming with ghosts, and they are wailing loudly. If you listen to them, you'll go insane. We also have Smokeshrooms, Manticores, and Gargoyles. It's a fun place, as you can see!»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«There are many villages like that in Umoir. Maybe the monsters chased the people out, or maybe they left themselves. The river burst its banks, the ground sank, or there was a poor harvest, and people moved to another place. Who lived here and why they left - there's no one around to tell.

First of all, beware of the Satyrs. They are strong, brave, and most importantly, you don't have to fight them. Give the Agitated Toads and Wolfbasts a wide berth, too. Not scared? That's fine - you'll have time for that when you run into the undead and the Gazebo in the city!

The undead from the city rarely wander in here. But there are plenty of living monsters. Mutant Toads, Corpse Eaters, and Reed Hydras. Something to fit any taste, as they say.»

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

"This temple is the oldest of all. It stood here in ancient times, even before the Cataclysm. They praised the Foremother who had power over fresh and salt water... There's still plenty of water here, but it's foul and toxic. If we get rid of the monsters and figure out how to make the water clean again, I'll travel all over Umoir with a bag, collecting money for the restoration of the temple. We can't leave the shrine in ruins!

This is where the Forestfolk have lived for centuries. When trouble came, they went crazy and turned into Elmclaws. But don't fear them. Be afraid of forest witches that are hiding in the woods. If one catches you, being cooked alive is not the worst thing that can happen to you!

They say when the city was alive, people from all over the region came here to pray for good health. Now, you see, the temple is in ruins, and its parish are the undead. Of the living, only animals remain - Carpetfish and the like. Though that fact doesn't really fill you with joy."

That's what my brother who's overseeing this area has said:

«The Ridgeline is probably the last place in the area untouched by the Blight, marauders, or vampires. But the place is no longer as quiet as it used to be. You can’t sit by the waterfall and think about eternity. Minotaurs, Satyrs, and Werewolves gathered here from all over the region. And they are not happy to see us here.

The most formidable are the Satyrs, especially when they're drunk. Besides them, it's the usual forest creatures: all sorts of mantes, spiders, Wolfbasts... No ghouls, no blighted things - it's a blessing!

All the forest dwellers have gathered here: the Minotaurs, the Werewolves, and the Spiritwoods... You know what? Just stay away from that place, don't disturb them. They're not really monsters, they just don't get along with humans. We need to be friends, not enemies - who knows, maybe we can defeat the Blight together! And beyond the watershed, it's the vampires' domain. Don't show them any mercy!»
And each is the size of a cat... How would I go home?

My father taught me this: I must please all and everyone - the host of house I would live in, the boss I'd work with and the man that would keep my clothes clean, the sweeper of the yard, and, just in case, his dog to win its love and kindness.

Secret labs... Any secret the Committee is trying to hide eventually comes out. Everybody knows our research program is having issues: something always explodes, or leaks, or just fails. But the more classified info, the more gossips that are spreading all around the Astral, deeper and deeper all the time. Now there's a reflection of the horrible rumors ever spoken about the lab: mad scientists, cultist spies, inhuman experiments, deadly machines and crippled test subjects, all the things that could ever be born by a sick imagination. So if you ever happen to come across a scientific laboratory behind iron gates and make up your mind to land - I hope you've got nerves of steel...
h: Ask about the reflection of Lab 731

t:
A weird place... I'm not sure if it exists for real, or if it is a vision, a mirage. It is covered with thick woods and deep swamps. All sorts of creatures dwell there, both sentient and not. I've seen kikimoras, satyrs, even a talking fox! On top of that, the place is swarming with ghosts. They are mostly Kanians - they look alive, but they are not. They all serve the mistress of that land - spirit Ziva, half-bird, half-human.

It used to be a quiet place, and the mistress was very sweet. But recently I heard from other travelers that something terrible had happened there - either a romantic heartbreak, or a curse... I suggest you don't approach Iriy without holy water and charged cannons.

Greetings!

I've been to the Astral far and wide. And I'm still up for more travels! I'll gladly share my knowledge with you.

How did you know about that?
It is a restricted information! Committee will punish anyone for disclosing it!
Well, once you have learned about the heretics, I'll share my knowledge with you. But don't tell anyone!
Heretic Refuge is a spot on the reputation of the Arisen, as these dangerous lunatics came from their nation.
A bunch of Arisen mages once came to denying the divine nature of Nezeb, Tensess and Skrakan. They believed that all beings are governed by four elements: Fire, Earth, Water and Nature. They turned so obsessed by their heresy, they didn't want to listen to the voice of sense. They hated everyone who didn't share their believes. Eventually they became involved in a series of infamous murders, so the Committee outlawed the sect.
Heretics seized a ship and fled into the Astral depths. Over the years they were almost forgotten, and their case was closed. But recently one captain told me of an adventurer who was unlucky to find heretic refuge somewhere in the Astral. He barely escaped! His ship was scorched with fire, a huge stone punched a hole in its cargo hold, its sails were covered with mold, and half of the crew turned into ice statues...
If you encounter the Heretics, remember that they are crazy murderers. No doubt they will try to kill you at all costs!

Hunting for treasures, are we? He-he... You won't find any there! All you'll find is sand, the scorching sun, the heat and scorpions nestled in the ruins.
A Historian friend of mine once told me that there once was a huge observatory there, where June priests studied the movement of the sun and stars, composed solar and lunar calendars and extremely detailed horoscopes. But these days the observatory temple is nothing ruins half-buried in the sand.
Quite recently wormfaces returned to the Tlalkoa Ruins. They cleaned some of the halls and fixed up old war golems, and now they guard the ruins zealously against trespassers. From what I understood they are led by someone named Mirage, who seems to be in dire need of something in these ruins. So dire that he won't hesitate to kill anyone who enters the old temple. I was lucky enough to escape with my wife, or my bones would have long been dried and polished by the hot desert sun...

Once, sailing deep in the astral, I happened to stumble onto an island of eternal winter. It is ruled by Yaver Artea, an Arisen gone mad who calls herself the Snow Queen. What a nasty broad she is, I'm telling you! It's a miracle I got out of there in one piece. The Snow Queen's pastime of choice is kidnapping people and posing riddles to them, and those who give the wrong answer are turned to ice statues! In her ice castle Yaver Artea has a suite of rooms full of ice statues that used to be orcs, gibberlings, arisen and humans... Her heart is just as cold as her ice throne!
That frigid bitch was about to make an ice statue of me - the fact that I escaped is a miracle in its own right.
Yaver Artea must be stopped! If she were just killing people that'd be one thing - you simply take a trip to the Purgatory, rest up, come back out - no big deal. But she's making statues out of living beings! Imagine a human standing there, unable to move or breathe or even close their eyes. For a year, two years, a decade... Argh, what a nightmare! No, such coldblooded torment must not go unpunished!
But getting to the Queen won't be easy. Freeze, the mad werebear shaman, is a loyal guardian of his queen's peace. Rumor also has it that during the strongest snowstorms a huge bear named Cold appears on the island. As to whether that's true or not, I'll leave that up to you to find out!

Oh, that is a very interesting place. And a dangerous one, too!
The Land of a Thousand Wings is a pile of rocks and ancient buildings gone to seed ages ago. Three islands are interconnected via thin bridges that offer a breathtaking view. The Land of a Thousand Wings is only inhabited by creatures that can exist there and not risk dropping into the astral at any moment or breaking their necks on mountain sides. I'm talking about aviaks and harpies.
As I understand it, aviaks were the first to come to the Land of a Thousand Wings, while harpies invaded the island much later, leading to a massive battle. The upshot was that Koual the Stormbearer, the aviak leader, was able to tame the wild harpies. The Harpy Queen and he made peace, and now their races live in complete accord, helping one another in every way. In fact, something tells me there's more to the relationship between Koual and Olivia the Temptress than just politics... But that's irrelevant.
When I visited the allod a few times, I was always surprised by Koual's wisdom and agile mind. He even managed to tame a wild manticore living in the ruins of an old temple! But in recent years the aviaks have shut themselves off from the rest of the world, having accused the League and Empire of greed and folly, and vowed to make swift work of any who would risk coming to their land. I don't know what triggered such unexpected hatred towards other races, but maybe you could find out? If you really intend to go to the Land of a Thousand Wings, however, you had better prepare yourself for battle!
h: Ask about the Land of a Thousand Wings

t:
Fenia's Island? Ahh, that's the old Kanian Fortress, in which those, what do you call them... fenimists, is it?... have settled! Or is it feminists? In short, those women who believe that men insult and oppress them, which has driven them crazy. You tell me - have women ever been insulted in the Empire? It is in the League that people are wild and uncultured - they even have a saying that "chickens are not birds, women are not people." But here they are people indeed! But still, our Imperial girls regularly run off to this abode.... I don't understand why they are so up in arms against men?! Anyway, listen further.
Their leader is this Fenia, a crazy witch who has declared herself the incarnation of a deity and the protector of women. She declared that all the evil in the world comes from men, and she decided to wage merciless war against us, men that is! And if that wasn't laughable enough, she found some numskulls that believed in her! Or to be more precise, it was laughable until all the men on the island died, and the parts of their bodies, well - the body parts that are important to men - were... You know what, I don't want to talk about that. My friend Afanasy Nikitov was there, he saw it all with his own eyes. He spoke of such horrors... It was a miracle he survived!
Anyway, now there are no men in the Cloister. But there is, however, a gang of girls of all races who have become crazed without male attention and who are fanatics to the core, and are ready to rip any man that might set foot on the island to shreds. It's a paradox - they hate men, but without men they grow wild. No, I'll never understand women. Especially the type of women that grab a sword for no reason and try to chop off your most valuable asset. Ahem. I was talking about your head, not what you were thinking!

Is there no end to what you know?

Frankly, it is not an island at all. It is a giant turtle that eternally swims through the Astral. It is so enormous that a whole village lives on its back! Rather, lived...

You see... Have you heard of demon henchmen? Demon-worshipping cultists? So here is the story... Two Kanian noblemen, the Zalesky brothers, decided that the current authority did not suit them, and they can achieve a more appropriate position among noble Kanians, with the help of demons. Aidenus quickly found out about the treachery. The brothers gathered their militia, loaded up a ship and fled. And so their eyes saw the Turtle Island as it slowly swam through Astral space. They moored their ship. Peasants saw the noble ship and kindly welcomed the renegades, who then murdered their hosts! Save for several hunters, who managed to escape in the Astral. They were picked up by a Kanian ship belonging to my friend, Afanasy Nikitov. He was the one who told me the story.

As I understand, these demon worshippers want to submit the flying turtle to their will. Imagine if they succeed! Everyone will be at risk, not just Kania. So if someone were to put those cultists down like the mad dogs they are, I'd thank that hero!

I've only got a little information brought to me by the Imperial Scouts.

I'd had no idea this Isle even existed before the Committee officials started interrogating me about deeper layers of the Astral and the Isles I knew. It happened like this: an Imperial Scout ship came across an uncharted Isle in one of the sectors. The captain took a few pictures with a ferrotype camera, described whatever he saw through his optical devices and sent out the urgent message to the capital. The message said that the captain had taken a decision to land and explore. Nobody has seen him since.

He disappeared because of the message he had sent, as far as I can gather. You see, the island is called the Jail, and it is indeed a jail belonging to the Overlord! Pictures show exhausted prisoners locked inside lightning domes, and there are passages blocked with stasis fields. The whole perimeter is patrolled by the Overlord's servants and battle machines such as the Overlord's Eye - you may have seen them at the Citadel. The island is secured against any invasion by Overlord's Thrones. What's more, in the pictures there are creatures identified by our experts as high-ranked Wormfaces. Their theory is that it's the Wormfaces that run the Jail, which is a bit weird, because they betrayed the Overlord.

Out of all this I can draw one certain conclusion and make two guesses. I conclude that the Isle is the Overlord's Jail where some adventurers are imprisoned. Guesses are as follows, first, the Wormfaces managed somehow to bend the Overlord's servants to submission, and second, they're willing to stay low and out of sight, so I guess we'll never see the ship’s crew again. I wouldn't recommend going there without one or two battleships to assist you. There are secrets you just never want to reveal...

I don't know much about the jungle of Mboa-Mboa. We once traveled really far, into the deepest layers of the astral, and were just about to turn back, as we noticed a land on the horizon. We went closer and were blown away by the beauty! It was all green, bloom and blossom, butterflies fluttered about, monkeys jumped from tree to tree... It was paradise! At least, it had seemed to be until we set foot on dry land. But there - good gracious! I have never seen such hungry beasts! Enormous snakes, crocodiles the size of canoes, giant bloodsucking mosquitos. Did we turn on our heels! In our fright we ran right into a settlement of aborigines. They almost had us chopped to pieces, little evil bastards!

As soon as we escaped them, we stumbled into Draconids. They decided to invite us to dinner... to be dished up as a main course! So, we ran back twice as fast! We jumped on the ship and set off immediately...

I'm not setting a foot on that island again! To hell with such cruises!
h: Ask about the jungles of Mboa-Mboa"

t:
That isle is not particularly noteworthy. I don't even know much about it. Seems to be a Kanian allod. Dobrinya Velikov, a mage-conjurer, rules it. He calls himself "Great", although I have my doubts as to his ability to maintain a grip on the isle. Not a pleasant fellow by any stretch of the imagination... Huffs and puffs as if he were truly great, while in reality he's nothing more than a county fair magician!
There was a rumor that long ago a young magician named Alla miraculously ended up on the isle without any ship. Seems like some magical twister picked up her house, along with her dog and a nail file... On the island, Alla met strange but friendly creatures: a talking lion, an ancient lumberjack golem and a reanimated scarecrow. Together with her new friends, Alla found herself at the center of incredible adventures. In the end, she found the local mage who sent the would-be sorceress back home. Though if you ask me, I'd wager that the cause of this adventure was a bottle of fortified liquor, her huge impressionability, as well as a thirst for sensationalism among gum-beating scribblers, not a twister!

Ah, yes, I know about that isle. Why wouldn't I? I was there a few times. Not a bad place... if you are resigned to deal with continuous quacking! There is a Kanian village there, in which every home has lots and lost of ducks. They salt, bake, cure and sell ducks. I even have a duck feather pillow in my cabin. You wouldn't believe the softness! It's like sleeping on a cloud... Alas, a misfortune awaited this village.
Have you heard about a recent escape from the maximum security zone? No? Strange... It was in all the papers!
A whole gang of criminals of various backgrounds, mostly orcs and goblins, killed the guards, hijacked a ship and escaped in unknown direction. They dubbed themselves the "Tribe of the Daring" and started to burn, pillage and destroy everything on their path. Very dangerous and cruel outlaws! They captured several of our ships, took everything that was not nailed down, and made the crew walk the plank. They destroyed an outpost and its guards in the far Astral. It was so horrible that Committee investigators came back with green faces, spewing profanities. And the last thing I heard about that gang is that they stumbled upon Duck River Run. Needless to say, this couldn't have been good for the locals. I'm afraid to even imagine the turmoil that's there now!
h: Ask about the Duck River Run

t:
Blood Countess... Bathing in the blood of young girls to retain her own beauty... Do you really want to hear this story? Frankly speaking, it's disgusting.
Blood Countess' real name is Yasskul Bathory. A friend of mine, Fedor Stablemanov, knew her personally and told me that she was a nice lady and a prominent researcher. But her appearance was a fad with her. Bathory, once the most beautiful of the rulers, was grasping any chance to regain the lost beauty. And, unfortunately, she found a reliable way...
With the ancient dark magic she managed to rejuvenate her body... and lost her human soul!
For killing hundreds of girls she was outlawed and sentenced to death, but she managed to escape!
A whisper goes round that Blood Countess has hid on one of the astral islands. There she has a manor with many well-trained and loyal servants and continues her horrible and indecent actions. Beware of Blood Countess, if you do not want to be one of her slaves and end up in a bloodless body on the floor of her laboratory.

I know about that resort. Though it's not so much a resort... more like an epic fail. As you know, scientists like to boast about their technology and play the role of nature tamers. That is why they wanted to build the resort on eternal ice. So they found an appropriate freezing islet, erected a dome and built a whole town underneath. Imagine... Icy wind is howling, but inside the dome birds are singing, green grass grows... Idyllic, so to speak.
However, our brainiacs did not account for a tribe of wild orcs that lived in the islet's caves. Those orcs mostly fed on mountain goats and mushrooms that grew there. And when Imperial engineers were building their dome, they cemented the underground stream. Due to lack of pure water, goats died, mushrooms withered and orcs had nothing to feast upon. Naturally, they started warring with the resort guards. But those guards were ferocious in their own right! All veterans. Perhaps they thought that some bigwigs were going skiing or something. Made the resort secretive. One step beyond the perimeter, they fire without a warning. They don't care whether you are Kanian, Xadaganian or the Holy Tenses himself. They'll kill you on the spot! Once I wanted to unload some goods from my ship, but those idiots opened fire. Can you imagine? They were firing at an Imperial ship, no questions asked! Almost killed me! I spat at those fools, turned the ship around and flew away far from that island. Devil knows what mysteries they are protecting, if Xadaganians are firing at Xadaganians without hesitation.

Seasons... It has been so long since we last saw them change, even before Sarnaut broke... There's an old tale that tells about a little girl that was kicked out of the house into a deep forest in the middle of winter by an evil step-mother. She was about to freeze to death, when she came across twelve brothers on a clearing in the woods. These were the twelve months, who used to gather together once a year to see each other and chat. She warmed up by their fire and saw quite a few miracles.
That's merely a tale, of course, but one of my friends once told me he saw a wonderful isle in the Astral. It looked like a glass sphere, with a wood in the snow, and a clearing, and a fire, and twelve young men inside. As he flew by, the snow melted, flowers bloomed, then the green faded and withered, leaves began to fall, and then it was winter and snow again. He tried to approach the isle, but it disappeared all of a sudden, and he could never see it again. Do you think the tale told the truth? Is there such a place? Are there still seasons and the months? Who knows...
h: Ask about the Twelve Brothers' Grove

t:
This is an ancient stronghold, it traces its history back into the past. It started with the cordon lines built here by the Kanians to protect against orcish raids long time ago. It has seen many sieges, was burnt to the ground, but rebuilt every time... When the World broke into pieces, the shard of the stronghold disappeared in the Astral, but a bit of it remained.
Demon Hunters discovered and restored it, so it has become one of the strongest keeps. Demons don't even dare to approach!

You know about Quiet Hills, don't you? What a nice place that was! Looking at this bucolic village, I always thought that, in the future, we could forget about squabbles with Kanians and live happily together. But fate had other plans... A curse awoke and ruined the village in Quiet Hills, turning all peasants into ethereal apparitions. And recently, while exploring a deep layer of this Astral, I stumbled upon a Quiet Hills reflection. It is hundred times more horrible!
The reflection did not have any curse. But the peasants suffered even worse... A necromancer appeared on that island and easily subdued it! Sarang Fravashi was the necromancer's name. He decided to experiment with Kanian peasants... And ended up killing everyone! He turned the whole population of Quiet Hills into decaying zombies and bare-boned skeletons! Scary stuff... I still shiver when I think about it! They were Quiet Hills, but now they are Dead Hills...

New adventurers know that where there are June ruins, there are treasures. Wise adventurers know that treasures usually mean trouble. However, the wisest have been to all these ruins and took care of both.
Is there anything left in Altan Tepek? We came across the isle but couldn't land there. We just flew around it and took a good look at it: It looks like a tropical forest, but it's frozen and covered in snow, and the wind rages through the place. Something seemed to move there, but I'm not sure what it was. Are you curious? Well, if you manage to land there, let me know what that was and why it's frozen!

Normally you can come across nobody but Demons in the Astral, but some time ago huge swarms of termites came from nowhere, invulnerable to the Astral or anything else. At first they attacked ships, and once they even made it to Nezebgrad!
One of the Free Traders entrapped a few, dissected their bodies and found meteorite dust inside. The smell of money made many sign on to find their nest. Alas, they found nothing but death. And can you imagine the size of their nest? Whatever riches they have in their stomachs, there is no way I’m coming near it.

You ought to know what happened in Irdrich. A powerful Zem necromancer, Tep, announced himself a god, and was about to put his foot on Sarnaut's neck with his army of mechanoids. The League and the Empire united their forces to crush him, and so they did. The remnants of Tep's army are still there in Sarnaut.
The rusty mechanoids either aren't aware of Tep's fall or turned away from him. So don't be surprised if you ever come across them in the depths of the Astral.

Thank Yasker, there are so many Imperial resorts in the world! All kinds of them! Libraries, cinemas, museums! Choose whatever you like. But no! Some prefer hot and forbidden pleasures!
So, there's this goblin, who set up a fight Arena on one of the isles. Very much like Demon Arena, only without demons. There's gambling, and drinking, and party girls, and smugglers, and assassins, and slave dealers... Shame. If you ever come across this isle, just turn your back on it. It's no good anyway.

Old Loam? Why do you ask? Look me in the eye! Don't lie!

Huh, I guess I can discuss state secrets with you. Of course I know that allod. There is nothing special about it, just a poor cold village surrounded by pine-woods. Probably, that's the reason why the Council has chosen it as a test site for their experiments. Spying on Kanian households! Surveillance operations! Intelligence! Oh, just like in the good old days...

Some strange things are happening to animals near Old Loam, and some of the villagers have gone missing - this all I've heard from the sailors. I suggest you avoid that isle and stay away from Council's business. Just one mistake, and they will have to kill you. That would be sad.

You don't doubt they are working for the benefit of the Empire, do you?

That's one interesting place. I haven't been there for a while... And I don't miss it.

Just several years ago Triplefield was a lively trading town. They sold all kinds of goods there - elven gems, peasant straw shoes, Kanian armor...

But then there was an outbreak of the undead - they exterminated the whole place, and very few managed to survive. They collapsed the single bridge that led to the town and settled in a small village, far away from the damned ruins.

Happily, the nearby elven enclave wasn't affected by the outbreak, and they helped the survivors put their life back on track. But still the former glory of Triplefield was gone for good.

I heard that the League Church had sent a squad of Inquisitors there, and now I am wondering what do those servants of the Light have to do with that Light-forsaken place?

Oh, Firefrost and its temple... It's an allod where severe frosts and burning flames co-exist in peace and harmony. A beautiful place! And what looks beautiful from the Astral, is most certainly deadly. Remember: do not approach Firefrost! Once only goblins and trolls used to live there, but now it's Elementals as well. They say there's also a mysterious spirit, born by the two elements, reigning over the allod. I wish I could see it!

If you're not afraid of Elementals and don't want to live forever, you can find yourself a good team and give them a fight. After all, it's an ancient temple, filled with untold treasures. They have to do someone good!

A real pearl of the Astral! It would make a nice place for an Imperial resort. But alas, this is not going to happen. The allod is occupied by hostile aborigines.

Initially the Lagoon was only populated by an Aviak tribe. We used to have stable trade relations with them. Honest barter trade - their skins and jewels for our weapons. An incredible generosity on our part! Everybody knows there are no better weapons in the whole world.

But then some pirates, whose names are unknown to us, assaulted the Lagoon, hoping to easily steal all our goods. But the Aviaks repelled their attack and robbed their ship instead. Apparently, they found some eggs on the ship and took them. Unluckily, those were lizard eggs. When the lizards hatched, they fled to the other side of the allod. Soon there was another aborigine tribe in the Lagoon.

Since then the Aviaks of the Tusky Lagoon became hostile to the "wingless". If you fly by, don't expect them to be friendly.

Don't you know about it? "East Overshoe - that's where we're going," traders used to say before sailing out to that trading city. Its citizens used to always talk in proverbs!

Once it was a rich and peaceful city. But you know, words have power. Every time they saw an arriving trader, they said: "Speak of the devil!" Naturally, one day a real devil's imp appeared. Now they are facing the music, so to say.

I flew by East Overshoe the other day - it's silent and empty. But who knows what's really going on there? Still waters run deep, they say!

Plaque City? Alright, I will tell you its sad story. They say, once it was a beautiful town, and the citizens lived in peace and prosperity. The trade was thriving, and the craftsmen were making good money, and everybody praised the Light and led a godly life.

Blissful places like that one are rare, and they are like thorns in the flesh of the evil. And so the trouble came. The city was stricken by a magical pestilence. A mighty necromancer killed the city rulers and released all sorts of terrible diseases. The sky went black, and the earth swelled with impurity! Some citizens tried to burn the pest; others seized the moment and descended to pillage.

Eventually, the curse got so strong that the city split away from the allod and dissolved in the Astral, and its name was erased from the memory of people. But sometimes it appears here and there to relive the terrible Day of Pestilence. Be careful, or the city will swallow you as well.

Forgotten Temple? What, may I ask, is it you are looking for in that cursed place? Believe me, anyone who comes there craves to forget it has ever happened to them.

It used to be just plain June ruins in the middle of an island which was of no interest even to Demons, but then Wormfaces laid their hands on the temple and kindled a fire which had been dormant for centuries inside of it. The island burned like a torch until it collapsed with an ice shard of another allod. Now half of the island is burning with scorching fire, and the other one is ice-cold. Also, it is swarming with aggressive Elementals, golem sentries and Wormfaces, who detest strangers.

However, there are some madmen among the Historians who wish to risk their lives for the sake of science. I heard an expedition, lead by Martine de Blizare, recently set out to the Forgotten Temple... No one has heard anything from them ever since!

Ravine of Shadows? Yes, I've heard of it, although I haven't been there myself. One Priden traveler told me that many years ago a shard of Howlem split off and drifted away, with a temple which stood upon it.

Then some Astral pirates told me about a huge piece of rock in the Astral with ancient ruins on the top of it. They thought they could stuff their treasuries in that place, but they ended up fighting their own shadows! Few of them escaped, and the curse is still haunting anyone who dares to come to the Ravine...

I heard this story about the place: a long time ago, on a far away island, there lived a powerful mage who loved to conduct various experiments. One day he created a crystal - an artifact of unprecedented power which allowed him to control attractive force and alter matter. But as it turned out, the crystal had a mind of its own.

People in the city next to the tower started falling ill and dying, and the sorcerer himself became more cruel and reclusive. He stayed in his tower and barely interacted with the residents. At some point he noticed that the crystal never left his hands, and that he reacted badly when someone got curious about it. The mage realized that the artifact was changing him.

He decided to destroy the crystal, but it did not work, because he continued to hear the call of the artifact. The mage then decided to hide the fragments at a great distance from each other in hopes of weakening the artifact so he could control it. He created three shrines where he buried the pieces of the crystal. After taking the largest fragment of the artifact, the mage locked himself in the tower. He thought he could find a way to destroy the crystal completely.

Exhausted and embittered residents blamed the mage. They decided to destroy him along with his tower but could not finish the job. Over time, the island became deserted. The city was reduced to swampy ruins, and the shrines holding the artifact fragments developed cracks and partially collapsed. They changed the minds of the forest dwellers, making them more aggressive. Wights, zombies and skeletons appeared in the cemetery. And it got suspiciously quiet in the city square, among the destroyed statues and buildings...

They say a trio of treasure seekers recently went there - a family of Gibberlings: Indy, Nathan, and Lara... Perhaps you'll meet them?

This allod is rather small and unimportant. Seven old Knights used to dwell there, together with a poverty struck Elven House, who escaped from Anna’s harassment. Years passed by, but then the ill fate got them: first the Leper corrupted the island, then the leader of the House brought a present to his wife, who, by the way, originally went from Kania. The present was an antique June mirror, a plate of black obsidian in a golden frame, a true beauty. However, it’s typical for the June treasure to bear dark surprises. To cut a long story short, the allod used to be quite unnoticeable before, and now it’s also scary as hell. But who knows, may be some hot shots find themselves brave enough to obtain the rare treasure!

Nawlad Jeer is a living legend. Although “living” doesn’t quite describe him. He’s one of the world’s greatest necromancers. He’s been dwelling in an isolated mansion for many years now, talking only to the undead. His villagers, on the other hand, are quite the opposite: cheerful, merry, always willing to talk. Very open for vendors and foreign goods! One of my friends, a merchant, has recently been there, and just as he started unloading his goods, he saw a crowd of people staring into one spot, not paying attention to anything else. And there was this fog, ghostly fog spreading around. He made it to flee, scared to death. If you are ever around, may be, you will have a chance to find out what that was.

This allod belongs to Nomarkh Iblis, a rich inventor. He’s famous, but not too much respected - he prefers working out fraudulent plots to developing new weapons. The last time he played his trick on Yasker himself, but the latter couldn’t swallow that, of course, and sent a whole squad of Imperial soldiers to Iblis’ allod. I have no idea how it all will end. The allod is well guarded and armed. You can go and watch the show.

Don’t even ask. This allod is top secret. Neither you nor me should be even aware that it exists. Oh, all right, I love gossiping, I’ll tell you what I know. The Dead City revealed some technologies, that were gathered and moved for testing to this very allod. They wanted to open some Gates, don’t ask me what that is, I don’t want to know. You’re asking why? Because all staff was urgently evacuated from the allod recently, the whole sector closed and isolated, entrance prohibited! Oh, this is so exciting! But too risky, I wouldn’t go there myself. Sure, you can, why not. Tell me what you’ll have seen there, alright? Promise?

This prosperous mine used to belong to Umoir traders. In fact, it’s Mistress who rules the allod, within and without. It’s her good will to share the riches. Evidently, people got her angry with their greed or disrespect. In any case, there are wild beasts now, where the settlement used to be. I’m too scared of the Mistress, so I wouldn’t go there myself!

This allod had always been nothing but a naked stone, no life, no plants. But recently it magically transformed into a blooming land with rivers, trees and homes. I docked, and discovered amazing creatures I had never seen before. They look much like Gibberlings, but not at all Gibberlings. They’re fluffy and have big ears, very cheerful, but a bit twitchy. They say there’s another tribe beyond the mountain, and the war is about to break out. I appealed to the Light, and they only looked weird and hurried to say goodbye to me. That’s really an enigma!

This is the most widely known pirates’ nest in the world! It attracts all kinds of scum from all over the universe! Feint the Greedy himself moved there before he died. People say, that’s where he buried his treasures. But it’s the old story. The news are more troubling, however. One of my acquaintances, a decent gentleman, was about to stop by and push off his, so to say, goods, and all he saw was a wrecked fort, plumes of smoke and purple tentacles over it. So there is nothing good about the place, I tell you.

I’ve been there. It’s a nice place: green forests, fresh springs. A settlement in the middle with a tall wall around it, a temple in its center and nice citizens. Good place to visit and trade, you know. The locals suffer from the thieves, but they’re rich enough to hire someone to deal with them, right?

That is one curious inquiry. Have you any idea, that you could be easily put to prison just for asking such a question?

See, even after the Cataclysm some of the Xadaganians refused to recognize Nezeb's authority. When the industrial revolution began, a few isolated allods, where Xadaganians resided, declined to accept the new doctrine, and went on living up to the old rules. Dersaadet is just the place. So to say, a shard of the ancient Empire, lost in time.

They don't trust in the Light, don't worship the Trinity Church's saints. Instead, they pray to their Almighty in mosques. Mustafa al Muhad, the sultan of Dersaadet, possesses unlimited power. Anyone, who confronts him, faces his loyal janissary and wise Vizir's magic. However, if you come to Dersaadet with peace, you will be welcomed, wined and dined!

What would like to know?

These islands are for heroes who are ready to travel to the Holy Land but not yet ready to explore Irdrich.

(For players of levels 23 - 51)
h: Find out about nearby islands in the explored astral plane

t:
What would like to know?

These islands are for heroes who are ready to travel to Irdrich but who have not reached the maximum level yet.

(For players of levels 51 and above)
h: Ask about faraway allods in the explored astral
Ask about the allods in the Mysterious Astral

t:
What would like to know?

These islands are for heroes who are ready for the most difficult adventures with a Hero's Compass.
h: Ask about heroic adventures in the Mysterious Astral

t:
At ease, soldier!

They must have confused you, eh? Your face says it all. You must be tired of all those divine designs and intrigues. Well, I'll have a task for you...

At ease, soldier!

They must have confused you, eh? Your face says it all. You must be tired of all those divine designs and intrigues. Well, I'll have a task for you...

The Orcs are rebelling on the Izune Allod! Just think! While we are fighting for all of them here, they are robbing, pillaging, and killing common folk, and no one can bring them to justice?

Yes, Yasker wants to resolve the whole matter peacefully, but you and I both know that the only way to resolve it is to go there and show them what's what! The sure-fire way!

Ahem.

Young people, idling about? While we're so busy here.

Ahem.

Young people, idling about? While we're so busy here.

Who do you think rules our world? The Conclave of the Great Mages? Or the governors of the allods? Generals of the Empire? Ancient sorcerers? Almighty gods?

Or is it the Tycoons, huh?

It's close, but it's not the correct answer. Our world is ruled by money. Crystals or gold - it doesn't matter. But try and imagine one gold coin. And now imagine a billion of them - it's our company's weekly turnover. That's the real power that rules our world.

Why the long face, young manlady? Are you upset about what these two fools, Aidenus and Yasker, said to you? Never mind all that. What do they know? I wouldn't trust them to sweep the floor.

The Tycoon Club is quite impressed with what you have achieved in Eden. It's not about the Ambrosia, no. Information is what's important - it's worth something on its own.

We see huge potential for growth. Our world is too cramped for the Free Traders already, and the Star Trail seems to be the perfect solution.

We've heard of your exploits on Isa, young manlady! Well, a newly discovered allod is wonderful news. I'm sure the Gibberlings will appreciate the advantages of doing business with the Free Traders. After all, we have much to offer.

Despite the political perturbations, our field of activity is growing both outward and inward, since Sarnaut still has places that remain unexplored...
Hi there! Well, when are we moving?

Damn it! I've been exposed... May the devil take you and your Resistance! Go on gobbling mushrooms in a cellar! Me, I'll take my eternal life from Master, which I'll spend lying around on a beach! Don't you get it? You think Baranov and I are the only ones? Half the Resistance thinks the same, they just lack the courage to claim their own! Later, losers!
Excellent idea! Staying here is no longer possible. I'm going to pack up my basic belongings.
h: Talk about moving the Refuge to the Dump.

t: You see, the closer we are to the Seal, the faster my powers grow. A constant stream of magic flows directly from it. I’m beginning to understand why the Conclave wants to harness that power.
The light of my flame guides us through the Astral!

Hmm. Interesting. I noticed that streams of incredible power flow out of it across the Astral. It appears the Citadel itself is the center of a magical network... if you can call it that.

And trust me, even the Conclave at the peak of its power could not have created something like this. And now we need to destroy all this? Interesting mission.
h: What do you think lies ahead?

t: Some say the world will burn, and others think it will freeze over.

Ah, you’re back! I thought we would meet again...

I must admit, you aren't parasites after all, since you were able to defeat me...

Don’t worry, this time I’m on your side. You and your methods... I don't sympathize with you, but I like darkness even less.

In the darkest night, burning fire light!
h: What can you say about what happened?

t: Fire purifies all and brings peace.

The Great Mages have always speculated about things lying beyond Sarnaut. During the Cataclysm, many works were written about this, even though such research was prohibited by the Conclave. Skrakan himself was extremely interested in this...

And now we know what's there.

Many other worlds where great forces wage their war. And we became part of this war.

We weren't given much choice, however. It looks like no one in these worlds has it.

What do we do? How do we proceed? Alas, I can't give you any advice... It's up to you.

Hello! It's good to see you again after all that dark business on Jigran! Nihilists who fought on your side... What an amazing force they had gathered! I'm afraid the Order of Stars might be behind this. They once fought the Great Mages...

Though maybe it's not them but the spirit of rebellion in Sarnaut. The Elves and Gibberlings are drifting away from Kania, the Arisen Zem are angry with Xadagan which failed to protect them, the Orcs are actually rebelling! But the most dangerous are those who seem meek and quiet...

Goblins! Who knows what they'll get up to? Goblins are decent mages and technicians... It's a threat no one has foreseen. It might be deadly!

They say magic is a sword without a hilt. You can't hold it without it affecting you. But even without a hilt, a sword is still a sword. And you can use it to defend yourself.
We're moving out soon. Danas and Naira will strike from the flanks.
You will regret this! You will, eysh!
Told you, we'd see each other again. Honestly, I was more of you than the fight you started here.
Oh please, hold the drama. Told you, we'd see each other again. Keep doing what you've been doing.

What do you think I'm doing here? Approaching the final stage of my plan, of course.

You've got something that's mine. Namely, a unique mystic orc, trained to be a Great Mage and able to guide me along the Star Trail.

I'm here for my property.

By the look on your face, I can't have it... and that's a quandary. I could absolutely neutralize all of you, so to say, including Eladia. But it'll take time, and I'm in a hurry. Here's the deal: I'll ask my Draconid friends to stop crashing the place, and you will keep me company in my journey.

As a bonus, my loyal friends will help you repel attacks of other... contenders for leaving this world.

Oh, and of course, I shall switch the station back on to feed the Gates.

Tell that to Eladia. She seems to be the decision maker here, am I right?
Raging flame, indomitable element! What could be more powerful than flame? Darkness and flame will create the eternal union!

h: Do you have something for me?

r483381.s: Priestesse of the Church of Light

t: Do you want to just ride our bird, or go to a particular place? No problem! Just one snowflake, and Roc will take you anywhere you want!
These records are of great value. Here, let me help you master the secrets of your profession.
My name is Flint and I'm the mining trainer. Speak now or go away!

Where is this Natasha?! What is she doing, the parasite? Is she gossiping? Complaining about her family? Samovar is not ready! Table is not set! And where is my wife, Vasilisa? That useless Vaska, that pig!

Both the League and the Empire were too weak to stand against the Darkness! Even Hiero... even Hiero yielded and fell prey to doubts. But we, the Paladins of the Cleansing Flame, doubt nothing! We will cleanse this world with fire!
I'm not a trader, but I have a way of coming across very rare goods. I can also help you find the right customers for your own valuables!
h: I need to sell you something in secret.

t: Yes... this is exactly what my clients are after. Oh, here they are!
Only got pike. No other fish. Woe!
My fishing net is empty. Just weeds and mud. Fish gets scared and goes away. Spirits are angry with us.

It's better without lake monsters! Now that we banished them, the sun is shining once again. And there's plenty of fish. I wish we could get rid of pikes. They eat down smaller fish! Soon there won't be any for us.
Um, well... See, there's plenty. Just take it. The river is full of it.
Hello there! How can I help you?
Keeper, I heard you needed a sparring partner to put your strength to the test.
If you need me again, you know where to look.
Is there a fortress that bullets can't reach?
